title: Greedy Best-First in Reykjavík: Fast Route Magic
description: Watch Greedy Best-First race across a street-map grid in Reykjavík (Miðborg), always expanding the node that looks closest to the goal. It’s a high-speed visualization of a heuristic-driven graph search that can find good routes quickly—without guaranteeing the shortest path.
ig_caption:
🇮🇸 Reykjavík (Miðborg) street-map sprint! 🗺️⚡

In this visualization I’m running **Greedy Best-First**: at each step, the algorithm picks the next intersection with the **lowest heuristic estimate h(n)** to the destination (think: straight-line distance from that node to the goal). That’s a classic **informed graph search** behavior—fast focus, heuristic guidance, and a priority queue that reshuffles the “most promising” frontier first. ✅

On a real road network (modeled as a graph where intersections are nodes and streets are edges), Greedy Best-First expands outward in a way that often looks intelligent—because it “chases the goal.” But it may still get misled by the map layout: since it doesn’t explicitly optimize the total cost so far (unlike algorithms that use g(n)+h(n)), the resulting path can be **quick but not guaranteed shortest**. 🧭📉

Want to see how different heuristics change the route shape? Drop a 🔥 and comment which heuristic you want next (Euclidean, Manhattan, or custom street-distance). And share this reel with a fellow coder! 👇🤝
fb_caption:
🚦 Greedy Best-First in Reykjavík (Miðborg): fast, heuristic-driven pathfinding! 🗺️⚡

This demo turns real street maps into a **graph** (intersections = nodes, roads = edges) and runs **Greedy Best-First**, always expanding the frontier node that appears closest to the goal using a heuristic h(n) (like straight-line distance). It’s a great example of how heuristic search can dramatically change exploration patterns—often finding a route quickly, while not always guaranteeing the shortest path.

If you like seeing graph algorithms come alive, follow for more visuals and share this post with someone learning CS! 💡
